message:
QUESTION:
How many agents should be rostered for the Monday 09:00-10:00 interval, and how does that compare with the 48 currently rostered?

DATA:
Inbound customer-service team, planning the Monday 09:00-10:00 interval.

- Forecast calls offered, Monday 09:00-10:00: 360. This forecast is already specific to Monday mornings: it was built from the last 8 Mondays and includes the usual Monday uplift of about 15% over other weekdays.
- Average talk time: 300 seconds per call.
- Average after-call work (wrap-up notes and logging): 45 seconds per call. Agents cannot take a new call during wrap-up.
- Average handle time (AHT) = talk time + after-call work.
- Workload in agent-hours = calls × AHT (seconds) / 3,600.
- Target occupancy: 85% (share of logged-in time agents spend handling calls). Productive agents needed = workload / occupancy.
- Shrinkage: 30% of rostered time is lost to breaks, training, coaching and absence. Planning convention: rostered agents = productive agents / (1 − shrinkage).
- Round the final rostered figure up to a whole agent.
- Currently rostered for this interval: 48 agents.
- Service-level history: on the last 8 Mondays, 09:00-10:00 averaged 61% of calls answered within 20 seconds against an 80% target, and an abandonment rate of 9%.

KNOWN FLAWS:
F1. [misreport] The data states the 360 forecast is already Monday-specific and already includes the Monday uplift. Applying 15% again double-counts it. CORRECTION: Use 360 calls, not 414.
F2. [omission] Uses talk time only. The data gives 45 seconds of after-call work per call, during which agents cannot take calls, and defines AHT as talk + wrap. CORRECTION: AHT = 345 seconds. With 360 calls, workload = 360 × 345 / 3,600 = 34.5 agent-hours. (The draft's 34.5 is right only by coincidence: two errors offset.)
F3. [calculation] Arithmetic error: 34.5 / 0.85 = 40.6. CORRECTION: 40.6 productive agents.
F4. [method] Applies shrinkage by multiplying by (1 + 0.30) instead of dividing by (1 − 0.30), as the planning convention requires. This understates the roster. CORRECTION: 40.6 / 0.70 = 58.0, so 58 rostered agents (10 more than the current 48, not 4).

EXTENSIONS:
- Workload-based staffing ignores queueing. An Erlang C check at 34.5 Erlangs (360 calls, 345 s AHT) shows 40 logged-in agents give about 80% answered within 20 s (39 give about 73%). This agrees with the 40.6 from the occupancy method and supports roughly 58 rostered.
- Sensitivity analysis: each 10% error in the call forecast moves the requirement by about 6 rostered agents (58 × 0.1), and each 5-point change in shrinkage moves it by about 4-5. Interval-level shrinkage for Monday 09:00 (e.g. with training barred) may differ from the 30% average.
- Use the 9% abandonment to sanity-check demand: handled calls understate offered demand, and repeat calls from abandoners may already be inflating the 360 forecast.

FINAL VERSION:
# Monday 09:00–10:00: Roster 58 Agents, 10 More Than the Current 48

## Calculation

| Step | Working | Result |
|---|---|---|
| AHT | 300 s talk + 45 s after-call work | **345 s** |
| Workload | 360 × 345 / 3,600 | **34.5 agent-hours** (34.5 Erlangs; the interval is one hour, so this equals agents busy on average) |
| Productive agents | 34.5 / 0.85 | **40.59** |
| Rostered agents | 40.59 / (1 − 0.30) | **57.98** |
| Rounded up | | **58 agents** |

With 58 rostered, productive staff is 58 × 0.70 = 40.6. Occupancy is then 34.5 / 40.6 ≈ 85%, which hits the target.

## Comparison with the current roster

- **The shortfall is 10 agents.** The current 48 is about 17% below the 58 required.
- **48 agents can't cover the workload at all.** After 30% shrinkage, 48 rostered gives 48 × 0.70 = **33.6 productive agents**. Work arrives at 34.5 agent-hours, so 48 would need about 103% occupancy (34.5 / 33.6), which is impossible.
- **The service-level history fits this picture.** When capacity is below the arriving work, the queue grows through the hour. Callers abandoning (9%) is the only thing keeping it bounded. So 61% answered within 20 seconds, against an 80% target, points to a lasting staffing gap rather than a few bad days.

## Service-level check (Erlang C)

The occupancy method doesn't directly test the 80% within 20 seconds target. So I checked it with Erlang C, using 34.5 Erlangs, AHT 345 s and a 20 s threshold:

| Productive agents | Rostered equivalent (÷ 0.70) | Probability of waiting | Answered within 20 s |
|---|---|---|---|
| 39 | 56 | 36% | ~73% |
| **40** | **58** (57.1 rounded up) | 27% | **~80%** |
| 41 | 59 (58.6 rounded up) | 21% | ~86% |
| 33.6 (current 48) | 48 | unstable | queue keeps growing |

- Erlang C also points to **58 rostered**: about 40 productive agents is the smallest number that meets 80/20.
- 58 rostered gives 40.6 productive, which is about 83% within 20 seconds.
- That margin is thin. At 57 rostered (39.9 productive), service level is right on the 80% line. Any extra shrinkage on the day would push it below target.

## Pitfalls avoided

1. **No double-counting of the Monday uplift.** The 360 already includes the ~15% Monday effect. Applying it again (414 calls) would inflate the need to **67** agents.
2. **After-call work is included.** Agents can't take calls during wrap-up, so the 45 s counts as workload. Using talk time alone gives 30 agent-hours, which works out to **51** agents.
3. **Shrinkage is applied by division.** Multiplying by 1.30 instead gives **53** agents and understates the need. The convention is ÷ (1 − 0.30).

## Caveats

- **The forecast may overstate true demand.** With 9% abandonment, some of the 360 offered calls are probably retries from callers who gave up. Once the interval is properly staffed, offered volume may fall slightly. Re-forecast after a few Mondays at the new staffing level.
- **Erlang C's assumptions are simplifications.** It assumes random arrivals spread evenly across the hour and that nobody abandons. If calls are concentrated around 09:00, the first part of the interval will need more cover than the hourly average suggests. Check 15- or 30-minute arrival patterns if they're available.
- **Monday 09:00 shrinkage is often above 30%.** Start-of-shift delays and Monday absence tend to push it up. At 33% shrinkage, 58 rostered gives only about 38.9 productive agents, below the ~40 needed for 80/20. If interval-level shrinkage data exists, use it. If not, treat 58 as the minimum.

**Recommendation:** Roster **58 agents** for Monday 09:00–10:00, an increase of 10 over the current 48. Both the occupancy method and an Erlang C service-level check support this figure. If you want a buffer against higher Monday-morning shrinkage, roster 59–60.
